engagement_background.objective: Christianbook engaged Treya Partners to quickly capture $655K–$1.7M in cost savings across high-value indirect spend categories, create incremental enterprise value for its private-equity sponsor, and help build a best-in-class, sustainable procurement capability.
engagement_background.scope_summary: The project targets roughly $18 million in baseline spend (~$15 million addressable) across 8–10 indirect categories including LTL/FTL freight, corrugated, packaging & shipping supplies, merchant processing fees, employee benefits, janitorial, marketing software and Ingram Book Group distribution. Low-spend/low-opportunity areas can be dropped, and additional work-streams in Advertising or IT may be added after further data collection; direct COGS items remain out of scope.
constraints_challenges: Long-standing incumbent supplier relationships (e.g., packaging, LTL) that create change-management sensitivities.
Potential lack of supplier responsiveness to data requests and RFP participation.
Risk of parallel or ‘side’ conversations by internal stakeholders that could weaken Treya’s negotiation leverage.
Limited line-item usage data; need to obtain detailed historical data from high-spend suppliers to finalize baselines.
Aggressive five-month project timeline tied to PE value-creation milestones and a mid-February 2025 completion target.

procurement_environment.data_availability: 12-month AP data (June 2023–May 2024) was provided and categorized; contracts and detailed usage files must be requested from individual suppliers and functional owners.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Vendor naming inconsistencies and partial line-item data require cleansing; no centralized contract repository, and some suppliers may never provide usage files despite repeated outreach.
